rv.q: It’s the most fun you’ll have in a Broadway theater right now.
This jukebox musical built around the songs of Max Martin is a candy-colored confection that manages to be both silly and surprisingly sweet.
What '& Juliet' lacks in foundation, it more than makes up for in sheer fun.

Either way, the play has two engaging, charming, vocal powerhouses in Courtney and Walker and, notably, it cleverly shifts the jukebox aesthetic into a much younger demographic, picking high-intensity music carefully targeted mostly to women and LGTBQ+ folks in their teens, 20s and 30s.
What saves “& Juliet” from being a lowest-common-denominator corporate byproduct is something else, something I never expected: wit.
If you were to adapt the feeling of getting day-drunk on cheap rosé for the stage, you’d get & Juliet.
It’s not that & Juliet is unenjoyable – it isn’t.
It's a shiny bauble, yes, but in the course of its two and a half hours the repetitive rhythms dull.
"& Juliet” will teach you, Romeo.
That may be why & Juliet, though often entertaining, also feels pretty disposable.
"& Juliet," the latest jukebox musical, is a delightful and witty reimagining of Shakespeare’s "Romeo and Juliet" told from a revisionist and feminist point of view.
The show’s terrific music numbers, fueled by high-powered vocals, give it a propulsive energy that’s impossible to resist.
If this sounds like a fun, enthusiastic ride, then just wait until the true performance begins!
The early zippy energy is a big plus.
All told, there is plenty of plot to go around, even if it does ask us to suspend a lot of disbelief along the way.

All things considered, the fashionable flare and youthful exuberance on display in “& Juliet” (as directed by Luke Sheppard and choreographed by Jennifer Weber) are often entrancing, and Martin’s songs (as arranged and orchestrated by Bill Sherman) are undeniably catchy.
The story seems largely guided by the songs rather than the other way around.
I'll cave to having been won over by its in-your-face enchantment.
Snack as heartily as you want on the poppy fun of & Juliet—but also be prepared to leave feeling like you haven’t really dented your appetite.
& Juliet is a visual and musical fest whose technical expertise deserves appreciation, even if you sometimes find it banal, monotonous, and unfunny.

Judging by the performance I witnessed, which had the added challenge of playing to some of the most jaded theater insiders, most are opting for the latter — and yes, against my most crotchety instincts, I include myself in that category.
By the time Szot sings “Everything,” this musical is less kitsch than schlock.
It comes pretty close to being “Fuckin’ Perfect“, the most fun in a Broadway theater right now, and by far the best jukebox musical Broadway has seen in a while.

All this while defying Lady Capulet (Veronica Otim, gorgeous, statuesque, & hilariously villainous) who plans on sending her daughter off to a nunnery. Hijinks ensue when William (Stark Sands) sabotages his wife’s good times by bringing Romeo (Daniel J.
& Juliet is an unmissable smash whose Broadway cast has recently featured TikTok star Cheryl Porter, Real Housewives of Atlanta’s Kandi Burruss, and NSYNC alum Joey Fatone.
Silly? Sure-but extremely entertaining, especially if you are familiar with the classic play and the popular music.
The Theatre is home to & Juliet’s open-ended Broadway run.

cn.t: Critics find this Max Martin jukebox musical a bubbly, exuberant pop confection that reimagines Juliet's story with girl-power flair. Most praise its infectious energy and fun, though some dismiss it as lightweight kitsch.
